why: eight mechanisms refuted, and every arm before this compared IMAGES that differ in many ways at once. Flash wait states are a register, so fetch timing can be varied on ONE image with no rebuild - the first arm this issue has had that changes one thing.
method: console '=<n>q' sets EEFC FMR FWS on both controllers, clamped 4..6. SystemInit sets 4 for MCK 78 MHz; lower would read flash faster than the part guarantees, higher is always safe. Visits interleaved 4,5,6,6,5,4,4,5,6 with 3 captures each.
verdict: CONFIRMED - the ninth hypothesis and the first to survive
findings: the three phase sets {75,219}, {16,251} and {12,138} do not overlap at all
FWS 5 gives phase 16 in 8 of 9, and gave 16 in 6 of 6 on an earlier visit
severity moves too, not just phase: FWS 4 stays inside the 25-code bound and both 5 and 6 breach it, on one image with no rebuild

this explains why the phase is a deterministic function of the image without being any of the eight things refuted: a different code layout means different instruction fetch timing through the flash buffer, which changes the gap between arming the DAC timer and arming the ADC trigger - and a phase IS that gap
consequence: #5's severity is effectively a lottery over code layout. That is why an unrelated commit - 398ac94, a console change - could push it past a bound it had sat under for weeks, and why 'which commit caused it' was never the right question.
not_claimed: that fetch timing is the only input - only that it is sufficient to move both phase and severity
any particular mitigation; nothing here was tried
